assessments.reasoning: The Boolean subsection identifies the two atom values and says there is no Boolean data type in the stated language model. Its built-in predicate recognizes true and false and rejects the example unrelated atom.

challenge.method: Check that a built-in recognizer can classify certain atoms without requiring a distinct data representation, using the third atom in the source example as a countercase.
challenge.results: Only the documented atoms true and false denote Booleans. The predicate example returns false for the atom ok. No inference is made about syntax-level aliases or arbitrary truthiness.

limitations: The conclusion applies to built-in value representation. It leaves typespec aliases, guard rules and other languages outside the claim.
